newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH FINMIN PROPOSES 35PCT ENERGY PRICE HIKE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH FINMIN PROPOSES 35PCT ENERGY PRICE HIKE.

text.p: The Czech Ministry of Finance has proposed to parliament a 35 percent increase in electricity and gas prices, effective July 1, the CTK news agency reported on Thursday.
CTK added that Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik told a parliamentary energy commission that prices for heating should be increased by 39 percent on July 1.
He added in his statement to the commission that a second "step" in price rises should occur on July 1, 1998.
He proposed that electricity prices then should rise by abuot 32 percent, while gas prices should be raised by 21 percent and heating prices by some 10 percent.
The Czech government has the final approval on any price increases in the energy sector, but it is routine for the Finance Minister to explain his proposals for pricing to parliament.
Kocarnik said he currently has no reliable calcuations on what level prices will actually cover costs.
Kocarnik did not say whether the price increase would include calculation of the country's value-added tax, which will rise to 22 percent from five percent on all energy as of July 1.

Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy has said he would like to see the entire increase given to energy producers, but Kocarnik has said he favours including at least part of the extra costs of the higher tax in the increase.
